post.summary: Resolve and provision a verified source identity
post.description: PROPOSED, outside the 74 canonical operations. Server derives tenant/environment/actor from a verified session and rechecks current permission, expiry and target visibility. Identity administration, owner eligibility, catalogue ownership and runtime authorization are distinct. Ownership never grants access. No handlers are supplied. Verify provider allowlist and source directory response using a server-held connection. Derive immutable issuer/subject, kind and display name from the verified source, never an email lookup alone or caller assertion. New principals receive no memberships. A unique issuer/subject conflict returns 409; only an exact idempotent replay returns the prior receipt.

post.summary: Disable or reverify and enable an existing identity
post.description: PROPOSED, outside the 74 canonical operations. Server derives tenant/environment/actor from a verified session and rechecks current permission, expiry and target visibility. Identity administration, owner eligibility, catalogue ownership and runtime authorization are distinct. Ownership never grants access. No handlers are supplied. Lock the principal and compare revision. Disable immediately even if it owns objects: retain all references, report ownership gaps, invalidate sessions/current grants and stop new protected admission. Never delete or cascade owners. Re-enable requires fresh source verification; revoked/expired grants are not restored. Remaining unrevoked grants require explicit review before enabling; return 409 if their review is absent. Protect the final active administrator or require a separately controlled audited break-glass path.

get.summary: List eligible human owners for an authorized target
get.description: Local runtime implementation; production acceptance remains pending. tenant_id and environment_id are optional selectors and must be supplied together. S01 revalidates the trusted principal's current membership in the selected context. Require the corresponding object create/write permission before listing candidates. Return enabled HUMAN principals from an admitted trusted issuer with current owner.eligible membership in this environment. For a create form, omit object_id but require create permission. Filter before pagination; do not expose invisible counts. Identity administration, owner eligibility, catalogue ownership and runtime authorization are distinct. Ownership never grants access.

200.description: Authorized metadata only; committed atomically for writes

post.summary: Transfer an accountable owner without transferring permissions
post.description: PROPOSED, outside the 74 canonical operations. Server derives tenant/environment/actor from a verified session and rechecks current permission, expiry and target visibility. Identity administration, owner eligibility, catalogue ownership and runtime authorization are distinct. Ownership never grants access. No handlers are supplied. Also require the object-specific write permission. Lock target, old/new principal and relevant eligibility grants in deterministic order; compare target revision and candidate eligibility at commit. Retain before/after owner and reason with command, audit and outbox atomically. Transfer does not approve objectives or confer reviewer/runtime access. For AGENT, lock and update both protected workload profile and internal service anchor in the same transaction, comparing expected_revision and expected_anchor_revision. A SERVICE request targeting an internal agent anchor is rejected; use AGENT transfer. The two metadata records remain one customer capability.

post.summary: Create an explicitly delegated capability grant
post.description: PROPOSED, outside the 74 canonical operations. Server derives tenant/environment/actor from a verified session and rechecks current permission, expiry and target visibility. Identity administration, owner eligibility, catalogue ownership and runtime authorization are distinct. Ownership never grants access. No handlers are supplied. Require an explicit current delegable capability/scope ceiling, bounded expiry and independent authorization for elevated grants. Server resolves the capability registry, service target and principal; reject wildcard escalation, self-escalation, SYSTEM/AGENT owner.eligible grants and unknown capabilities. owner.eligible is environment-local and uses service_scope=* but carries no runtime permission. Duplicate key/capability/scope conflicts return 409. Bind authorization_ref to a current independently authorized grant decision for the exact principal capability scope and expiry. A caller-supplied reference is not authority; verify its issuer, current validity and target match.

get.summary: List current tenant and environment contexts
get.description: Lists active tenant/environment contexts for the authenticated human identity from current, unrevoked, unexpired S01 memberships. The returned IDs are selectors only; they do not grant authority. S01 revalidates the trusted issuer, subject, principal status, and current membership when access is evaluated.

200.description: A bounded page of contexts available through current memberships

403.description: Identity is not currently trusted or valid

post.x-service-scope-enforcement: S02 filters service and agent reads to the delegated service, requires a matching scope for service and agent registration, and requires global scope for journey reads, writes, and capability links because journeys are not service-scoped.
post.description: Issues a short-lived S02 token only after S01 resolves the trusted principal and confirms every requested capability against current membership in the selected context. The token binds the requested service target in its service_scope claim (the service ID when supplied, or * for global scope); S02 enforces that scope for service-bound agent registration. tenant_id and environment_id are optional selectors that must be supplied together; they never grant authority. If omitted, S01 uses the signed context claims.

403.description: Principal is not admitted or requested capabilities exceed current authority

get.description: Without tenant_id and environment_id, uses the verified token context. If supplied, both are required and are treated only as selectors; S01 resolves the trusted identity and rechecks active membership for the selected tenant/environment. Client-supplied values never grant authority.
